title: Kernel Negotiator + Slew-Rate Control for Stable v2/v3 Prefill Handoffs
creator: Asha Mirza
description: Introduce a Kernel Negotiator component plus a Slew-Rate Controller that jointly decide per-request kernel selection (FlashAttention v2 vs v3 variant) during prefill and the initial decode window. Goal: reduce oscillation between kernels under mixed workloads, avoid startup latency spikes and transient OOMs observed in recent rollouts, and provide a safe, observable rollout path for v3 in production.
acceptance_criteria: Canary rollout shows no >10% regression in p99 prefill latency compared to baseline (v2) on mixed long/short workloads
Rate of kernel churn (v2<->v3 switches) per request <= 1 for 99% of requests in steady-state
No increase in OOM incidents across canary hosts; workspace allocations remain within historical bounds
Graceful fallback path implemented and exercised by chaos test (force memory pressure) with automated rollback signal
Telemetry surfaces decision rationale (latency budget, mem_est, runtime_score) for every kernel decision
steps: Implement lightweight Kernel Negotiator module that consumes request_metadata (token_budget, expected_seq_len_histogram, tenant_tier) and host telemetry (available_workspace_bytes, recent_kernel_latency_profile)
Add Slew-Rate Controller: enforce a max fraction of switches over sliding window per GPU to avoid thrashing during traffic shifts
Integrate soft affinity table: prefer last-successful-kernel for a request fingerprint when safe
Instrument decision outputs (reason_code, score_delta, mem_margin) and ship events to telemetry pipeline
Create unit + e2e harness that simulates mixed bursty workloads with long/short contexts and varying quantization variants
Run canary on 5% capacity with automatic rollback thresholds tied to p99 latency, OOM rate, and error-rate signals
If stable, expand to 25% then 100% with staged gating
decisions: Use a scoring function that combines estimated decode latency and memory margin rather than a single heuristic metric
Prioritize memory-safe choices when mem_margin < 15% even if latency score favors v3
Slew-rate limit default set to 0.05 (max 5% of requests may change kernel per 1-minute window) to prevent oscillation; tuned in experiments
Make soft affinity TTL configurable per model family (default 30s), stored in in-memory LRU per host
Expose a debug flag to force kernel for individual requests for regression triage
risk_mitigation: Rollback hook: runtime receives a 'kernel-selection-frozen' flag from control-plane to immediately stop negotiation and enforce safe fallback
Automated chaos test that injects artificial memory pressure and verifies fallback correctness
Canary monitors for three signals (p99 latency delta, OOM count, kernel_churn_rate) and aborts rollout if any threshold breached
Keep nightly batch of workloads to compare token-throughput and correctness regressions between selected kernels
notes: Initial investigation (INC-2025-11-01) showed correlated p99 prefill spikes when v3 was enabled concurrently with microbatch warmups
Telemetry indicated rapid kernel oscillation during workload shifts, causing transient workspace overcommit and OOMs on T4-like nodes
Benchmarks: on long-context LLaMA-2-13B, v3 yields 18% token throughput improvement but increases workspace by ~22% for certain sequence splits
Design review feedback (2025-11-21): PM asked for explicit customer-facing rollout notes and an early opt-out toggle for Dedicated customers
Security review: no new surface, but telemetry includes per-request model fingerprints - scrub PII before export
open_tasks: Finish telemetry schema and ensure events are GDPR-safe (diego)
Tune slew-rate threshold via controlled A/B (asha+bench)
Add eviction-safe workspace estimator to mem_est (infra)
Prepare canary runbook and alerting thresholds (oncall)
Create customer communication draft for Dedicated tenants (pm)
Validate fallback under quantized model variants (qa)
Wire control-plane feature flagging for immediate freeze/rollback
